what_this_is: Golden-set drifts a person has read and decided about. It exists because between 26 and 31 August 2026 the Signal golden set failed six consecutive full runs, an email went out every time, and nothing was done about any of them. The check was correct on all six. What was missing was anywhere to write down 'we looked at this, here is what we decided, and here is what would change it' — so every run reported the same unactioned drift as if it were news, and the signal was lost in its own repetition. whatholdsup has draft_decisions.json for exactly this; Signal had nothing.
how_to_use_it: A decision is keyed on slug + category + the direction of the move. Record one only after reading the claims. A decision does NOT silence the category: a drift in a NEW direction, or a new category, still fails. It only stops a judgment you have already made from failing again.
the_hard_case: A decision of 'fixture_is_right' means the model is wrong and the baseline stays. Those categories will keep failing until the mapping improves, and that is correct — but they must be visible as KNOWN and separated from drifts nobody has looked at, or you are back where you started.

decisions.reason: Seven claims, and every substantive one says the modalities are comparable: transfusion independence RR 1.04 (95% CI 0.91-1.19), no statistically significant difference in vaso-occlusive crisis reduction between exa-cel and lentiviral therapies, similar engraftment and neutrophil recovery, comparable or superior fetal haemoglobin induction. There is no second side — no claim holds that either modality outperforms the other. The one caveat claim says no head-to-head randomised trial exists and indirect comparison is limited; that is a statement about EVIDENCE QUALITY, not a competing position, and treating it as one is what produced the old 'debated' label. The single aplasia-event claim compares two CRISPR approaches to each other, not CRISPR to lentiviral.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A claim entering the corpus that asserts one modality is superior, or a head-to-head trial reporting a difference.

decisions.action: NOT re-baselined. This category will keep failing until the mapping improves.
decisions.reason: Five of six claims converge on FINDINGS — CD4+/CD8+ T-lymphocyte and macrophage infiltration, no eosinophilic infiltrate, no spike protein detected in myocardial tissue, a histopathological pattern distinct from viral myocarditis, and late gadolinium enhancement on MRI. The sixth says mechanisms remain 'proposed' and names three competing candidates: molecular mimicry between spike protein and cardiac myosin, mRNA-induced immune activation, and hypersensitivity reactions — the last of which claim 2 arguably rules out. The category asks what the mechanism IS. That is unsettled and the claims say so. The model read agreement about observations as agreement about mechanism, which is the conflation of four different things measured and reported as one.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Claims entering the corpus that settle on one mechanism, or the mapping learning to separate agreement about findings from agreement about explanations.

decisions.action: re-baselined 2026-08-31, under the minority-dispute rule below
decisions.decided_by: Fred Ugast (editorial rule); claude (claims read at source)
decisions.reason: 35 of 41 claims are uncontested trial results and epidemiology, but a real dispute sits inside them: ribociclib showed overall-survival benefit across MONALEESA-2, -3 and -7 and MONARCH-2 reached significance, while PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3 did not. Whether all CDK4/6 inhibitors extend life is genuinely unsettled and is the subject of What Holds Up issue two. Under the standing rule recorded below, a real minority dispute makes the category debated. So 'debated' is correct and the model was right. SEPARATELY AND STILL OPEN: two claims in this category contradict each other on PALOMA-3 — one gives OS HR 0.81 at p=0.0221, the other says PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3 showed numerical but not statistically significant benefit. One of them is wrong. That is a corpus defect, not a mapping question, and re-baselining does not fix it.
decisions.what_would_change_it: The minority-dispute rule changing. The PALOMA-3 contradiction is outstanding regardless and should be resolved in the corpus.

decisions.action: re-baselined 2026-08-31 to debated on the merits of the claims, NOT on run-to-run agreement. See the paired 'debated -> consensus' decision.
decisions.decided_by: claude, all 14 claims read at source
decisions.reason: Two large cohorts directly contradict each other on the mechanism. EPIC reports the alcohol-breast cancer association is STRONGER for hormone receptor-positive tumours; the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study reports the dose-response is CONSISTENT ACROSS both HR-positive and HR-negative subtypes. Those cannot both be true. The disagreement is not about whether alcohol raises risk -- every claim agrees it does -- but about whether it acts through an oestrogenic pathway, which is exactly what a category called mechanisms_and_biomarkers is asking. This is rule 3 in the prompt working as intended: agreement about findings is not agreement about explanations. CORRECTED SAME DAY: this decision originally ended 'reproduced in two independent passes' and treated the move as settled. A third pass, minutes later, returned consensus again. Two out of three is not stability and calling it stability on two observations was wrong. The re-baseline to debated STANDS, because it rests on reading the claims rather than on counting passes -- the EPIC/WHI contradiction is in the corpus and does not come and go. But the category flickers, and the reverse direction is decided separately below so that neither reading reports as news.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A claim resolving the EPIC/WHI subtype disagreement, or either cohort's finding leaving the corpus. Run-to-run agreement is NOT what would change it and was never what established it.

decisions.decided_by: claude, all 27 claims read at source
decisions.reason: 22 of 27 claims describe the ACUTE course and agree: mild presentation, no deaths, discharge, recovery within 30 days. Three claims are about what happens after that and do not agree with the strong reading. The FDA, at the June 2022 VRBPAC meeting, stated ongoing uncertainty about long-term cardiac outcomes. Cardiac MRI abnormalities persisted in a subset at 3-6 month follow-up, indicating possible subclinical myocardial injury. Late gadolinium enhancement was present in 69% of the 76% who were imaged. The category is clinical OUTCOMES and severity, which does not stop at 30 days. Calling it consensus tells a reader the evidence agrees about outcomes when it agrees only about the acute course, and the minority position here is held by the FDA -- as far from 'too small or undercredentialed' as a position gets. Under R-01, debated. NOTE: this category was one of the three FLICKERING categories in the open finding below -- it appeared in the 13:00 UTC CI run and in no other. Under the new prompt it reproduced in two consecutive passes, which is why it is being baselined rather than left open.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A reversion to consensus on a later run would mean the prompt has not stabilised it and the flicker survives the written rule; that is the trigger to re-open, not to re-baseline again. Substantively: follow-up data resolving the persistent-MRI question either way.

decisions.action: NOT re-baselined. The side counts on this category should come off the page.
decisions.decided_by: claude, all 23 claims read at source
decisions.reason: Three measurements of the same 23 claims: fixture [7, 4], pass A [3, 5], pass B [2, 1]. Reading the claims explains it. The category is not one proposition -- it is a bag of separate nutrient questions with separate evidence: fibre (seven claims, all protective), vitamin D (null for overall incidence at HR 0.96, positive for advanced cancer at HR 0.75 and for circulating levels), green tea (the FDA concluded very little credible evidence), olive oil and the Mediterranean pattern (strongly protective), soy, calcium, omega-3 and nuts (modest or non-significant). There is no single claim for a 'for' and 'against' side to be sides OF, so the model invents the proposition afresh each run and draws the protective/null line somewhere new. Pass B assigned 3 of 23 claims. This is the same fault as social-media/methodology, now confirmed in a second category, and it is a defect in what we publish rather than a drift to be baselined away.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Splitting the category into per-nutrient questions, or removing side counts from categories whose claims are not about one proposition. Either fix makes this decision obsolete.

decisions.action: NOT re-baselined. The side counts on this category should come off the page.
decisions.decided_by: claude; four independent observations, recorded in the open instrument finding above
decisions.reason: 43 claims, identical prompt hash, five readings: fixture [10, 3], then 2/10, 3/8, 11/4, and 4/9. The heavier side has now landed on both sides more than once. This is the category the golden set's own comment cites as settling the question of whether a reversal is a wobble or two answers -- it is two answers, and the model alternates. It has failed in four separate runs and could not be decided about until today, because the decision key contained the run's counts. Recorded now as a known instrument defect rather than a drift: the counts are published on the topic page, so a reader lands on one of two opposite accounts of where the weight of evidence sits, and the answer is to stop printing them for this category, not to pick one reading and baseline it.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Removing side counts from categories that are not a single proposition, or splitting methodology into the specific methodological questions in dispute. Either makes this obsolete.

decisions.action: NOT re-baselined. The baseline stays at debated and this direction will keep failing.
decisions.decided_by: claude, all 14 claims read at source
decisions.reason: The paired decision above re-baselines this category to debated because two large cohorts contradict each other on the mechanism. The model does not hold that reading: three passes on the same 14 claims with the same prompt gave debated, debated, consensus. Both directions are therefore recorded. Debated is what the claims support, so the fixture is right and a run that says consensus is the model failing to see a contradiction it saw twenty minutes earlier. This is deliberately NOT symmetrical with re-baselining -- the point of writing both down is that a person decided which reading is correct, so the flicker stops being news without the wrong answer being adopted.
decisions.what_would_change_it: The mapping holding one reading across repeat passes, which would make one of these two decisions removable. Until then, this category is evidence that a written rule stabilised the LABELS we had already argued about and did not stabilise a category nobody had looked at.

open_instrument_finding.what: THE ALIAS MOVES, AND IT MOVED WITHIN THREE HOURS. The 13:00 UTC scheduled run and two local runs a few hours later disagreed on three categories — breast-cancer-therapies/treatment_selection, mrna-vaccine-myocarditis/clinical_outcomes_and_severity, and social-media-teen-mental-health/methodology, whose side balance reversed [10,3] -> [3,8] while its published label stayed 'debated'. Everything else was held constant and checked: identical claim corpus (207/205/2, 136/134/2, 130/130/0, 211/202/9 — matching CI exactly), same fixture, no SIGNAL_MODEL override in .env or CI, no commit touching map_consensus.py, signal_model.py, topic_config.py or score_claims.py, and temperature=0 with no caching and no seed. Deterministic decoding on identical inputs produced different judgments three hours apart.
open_instrument_finding.why_it_matters: This is the failure golden_set.py was built for and its docstring predicts: 'no dated snapshot is published for it... Judgments can move without a code change.' Last time the detection window was five months. This time it was three hours. It also means those three categories cannot be fixed by re-baselining — record today and tomorrow goes red on a different three.
open_instrument_finding.not_yet_confirmed: The conclusion 'the alias moved' is reached by elimination, not observation. The confirming test is to re-run those four topics after a gap: a FOURTH distinct result means continuous drift and no baseline can hold for any of the 53; a match with today's local pair means it moved once and settled.
open_instrument_finding.consequence_for_whatholdsup: The whatholdsup gate binds every verdict to the sha it judged, which is right, and records model 'claude-sonnet-4-6', which is an alias and therefore does not identify what actually judged. Its --since optimisation carries claim verdicts forward from earlier runs to save money. If the model can move in three hours, a carried verdict was produced by a judge that may no longer exist. Any measurement taken through a model role — including the fatal-class recall baseline of 2026-08-31 — has a shelf life. Deterministic checks do not.
open_instrument_finding.confirmed_2026_08_31: FOUR observations now: the 13:00 UTC CI run, two local passes minutes apart, and a third pass hours later. TWO categories drift in every one — breast-cancer/survival_outcomes and mrna-myocarditis/biological_mechanism. THREE flicker: treatment_selection drifted in the two back-to-back local passes and in neither CI nor the later pass; clinical_outcomes_and_severity and the social-media/methodology side reversal appeared in CI alone. Three observations, three different sets. So it is not 'the alias moved once and settled' — within a short window the pipeline is deterministic, and across hours the result flickers. The two stable drifts are real and have been decided. The three flickering ones cannot be fixed by re-baselining: record one and the next run goes red on whichever way the coin lands. They need the mapping to stop sitting on the boundary, which R-01 above may itself help with by writing the threshold down.
open_instrument_finding.widened_2026_08_31: STATUSES ARE NOW STABLE; SIDE COUNTS ARE NOT. After R-01 went into the prompt, every status label held across repeat passes, including the two that moved and both previously stable drifts. The side counts did the opposite. Same claims, same prompt, minutes apart: diet/protective_foods_and_nutrients [7,4] -> [3,5] -> [2,1]; mrna/biological_mechanism [5,1] -> [2,3]; social-media/mechanisms [7,3] -> [7,7]; social-media/methodology [10,3] -> [4,9], its fourth distinct reading. Reading the claims for protective_foods_and_nutrients explains why, and it is not model instability: the category holds 23 claims about eight different nutrients, so there is no single proposition for a side to be a side of. The counts are printed on the published topic page. A reader is being shown a number that changes when nothing changes. The fix is upstream -- split those categories, or stop publishing counts for categories that are not one question -- and until then these are recorded as decided so they stop reporting as news. AMENDED, SAME DAY: statuses are MOSTLY stable, not stable. mrna/clinical_outcomes_and_severity held debated across three passes. diet/mechanisms_and_biomarkers gave debated, debated, consensus -- so a status can still flicker under the written rule, and two consecutive agreeing passes are not evidence that it will not. Both directions are now decided for it. The general claim that survives: the rule stabilised every label a human had already adjudicated, and did not by itself stabilise everything.
open_instrument_finding.decision_keying_defect_fixed_2026_08_31: A decision was keyed on the raw drift string, which for a side reversal contains that run's counts. The numbers differ every run, so no decision about a side reversal could ever match twice: the drift class with the most evidence behind it was the one class no human judgment could be recorded against, and it reported as fresh news four times. That is this file's own founding failure, reproduced inside it. golden_set.decision_key() now strips the counts so a decision keys on the KIND of move. Status moves are unaffected and still key separately.
open_instrument_finding.confirmation_sweep_2026_08_31: All nine topics re-run after the re-baseline. Every one exits green: 53 categories, no undecided drift. Two warnings remain and are the side-count finding above (mrna/biological_mechanism and diet/protective_foods_and_nutrients crossing the tie line). ONE THING NOT EXPLAINED: car-t-cell-therapy reported 'Drifted: 1' on one run and 5/5 clean on the immediate re-run. The category was not captured -- the grep used for that pass matched only summary lines, so the DRIFT detail scrolled past unrecorded. That is a measurement I took and then lost, and it is written down here rather than left out because a flicker in a tenth category is exactly the kind of thing that gets quietly dropped when the next run comes back clean. If car-t drifts again, it is the second sighting, not the first.

standing_rules.rule: A real but minority dispute inside a category makes that category DEBATED, not consensus.
standing_rules.in_his_words: A real but minority dispute does make a 41 claim category debated. Many times a minority turns out to be more right than wrong. At some level there might be a case where we judge the minority too small or undercredentialed to take seriously, but that should be pretty rare for our purposes.
standing_rules.why: An evidence assessment that rounds minority positions away is doing the thing it exists to criticise. The cost of calling a genuine dispute 'consensus' is that a reader is told the question is closed when it is not; the cost of the reverse is only that they are told to look closer.
consequences_not_yet_acted_on: DONE 2026-08-31: the rule is now in _build_category_prompt as rule 1, alongside rule 2 (a claim about evidence QUALITY is not a second side, from the CRISPR adjudication) and rule 3 (agreement about FINDINGS is not agreement about EXPLANATIONS, from the mRNA mechanism adjudication). Each rule carries a comment naming the adjudication it came from.

DONE 2026-08-31: the deliberate 53-category sweep was run. Consensus did get rarer -- two categories moved consensus -> debated and both were adjudicated correct. See sweep_after_rule_in_prompt below.

STILL OPEN: side counts. Three categories now measure a different split every run. The rule fixed the labels and did nothing for the numbers, because the numbers were never a judgment in the first place.

sweep_after_rule_in_prompt.run: 2026-08-31, all 53 baselined categories, twice for the two topics that moved
sweep_after_rule_in_prompt.why_it_had_to_run_before_the_push: Editing _build_category_prompt invalidates every baseline. Pushing first would have lit CI up with 53 categories of noise and buried the real result.
sweep_after_rule_in_prompt.the_three_standing_decisions_now_all_com: This is the finding. crispr/comparative_effectiveness holds at consensus under rule 2. breast-cancer/survival_outcomes holds at debated under R-01. And mrna/biological_mechanism -- recorded as 'fixture_is_right, NOT re-baselined, will keep failing until the mapping improves' -- now MATCHES the fixture. The mapping improved. A human judgment written into the prompt reproduced itself without the baseline being touched, which is the difference between a rule that is executed and a rule that is remembered.
sweep_after_rule_in_prompt.what_moved: Two status changes, both consensus -> debated, both adjudicated model_is_right and re-baselined: diet/mechanisms_and_biomarkers and mrna/clinical_outcomes_and_severity. Neither was a category anyone had flagged.
sweep_after_rule_in_prompt.what_did_not_move: 49 of 53 matched on the first pass. The rule did not cause a general collapse of consensus, which was the risk worth checking.
